summary: The focused object-printing depth claim is refuted. Both versions can print parser-produced objects at every nesting depth the parser accepts.

assessment.necessity_reason: Parsing and printing count array and object nesting with the same limit. Every parser-produced object is below the new printer’s rejection threshold, so the old harness satisfies the frozen obligation.

before.requirement: Print a parser-produced object without rejecting a nesting depth accepted by parsing.
before.reason: The complete old object printer has no depth check, and the harness prints only a successfully parsed tree.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Parser dispatch sends container inputs to the guarded array and object parsers.
Object parsing rejects nesting at the limit.
Array parsing applies the same limit to mixed nesting.

after.requirement: Print a parser-produced object without rejecting a nesting depth accepted by parsing.
after.reason: The new object printer rejects a container only when its current depth reaches the limit. Parsing rejects that same container at that depth; array and object printing count mixed nesting consistently.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Complete parser dispatch routes container inputs through the guarded parsers.
Object parsing rejects a container at the printer’s threshold.
Array parsing uses the same threshold for mixed nesting.
Array printing uses the same pre-increment depth check.

assessment.comparison_reason: The old harness passes a successfully parsed tree directly to a printer on both sides. The added object check cannot reject an object solely for a depth accepted by this parser.
